title: kv-cache: improve memory management and spillover eviction to reduce fragmentation and page thrash
author: Asha Patel
body: Motivation: KV cache spillover and ad-hoc eviction have been a persistent source of tail latency and GPU memory fragmentation under mixed-workload traffic. Small allocations and frequent page migrations triggered by LRU-only eviction increase paging thrash and reduce usable KV density. This change introduces a memory-aware eviction and spillover manager that performs adaptive compaction, size-class aware eviction, and a background paging scheduler to smooth spike behavior. Key changes: 1) New memory_manager module (kv/memory_manager.{cc,h}) implementing size-class bins, per-bin defragmentation passes, and heuristic scoring that accounts for KV fragment count, lifetime, and reuse probability. 2) Spillover rewriting: rather than immediate one-to-one spill to CPU pages, spillover now batches low-value entries and writes compacted pages to the spillstore to reduce I/O and page table churn. 3) Eviction policy: hybrid LFU/LRU scoring with a decay term and explicit fragmentation penalty; configurable thresholds per-instance. 4) Background scheduler: continuous low-priority defragmentation and paging tasks that operate when GPU utilization is below a threshold to avoid interference with inference traffic. 5) Telemetry: new metrics exported to Prometheus for per-bin fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs, spill_batch_size, and eviction_reasons. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on rtx8000 and a2-highmem instances show 12-18% median latency improvement for long-context chat workloads and 25-40% reduction in page-faults under stress tests. End-to-end throughput improved by 9% in our 512-concurrent-stream canary. Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is gated behind a feature flag KV_MEMORY_MANAGER_V2 (off by default). The PR includes a migration path for saved spillstore pages and a safe fallback to legacy eviction. Tests and CI: unit tests for scoring heuristics and integration tests against the perf-canary harness were added. Stress tests validated no regression in cold-starts. Rolling plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters with canary on 5% of traffic, monitoring compaction runs and tail latency; automatic rollback if tail P99 increases by more than 20%. Related work: follows up on earlier defrag/spillover PRs (see PRs 127345, 160530, 101235) and Linear tickets ENG-3421 and ENG-3589. Change list: code additions (~1.2k LOC), new metrics, docs update in docs/kv-cache/eviction.md, and a smoke-test script for ops. Please review the memory manager API and the decay constants; I included conservative defaults.
commits: Implement size-class bins and compaction pass
Batch spillover writer and spillstore compactor
Hybrid LFU/LRU eviction score with fragmentation penalty
Add background scheduler and gating by util threshold
Prometheus metrics and docs for kv memory manager
Add unit and integration tests; fix race discovered in scheduler
files_changed: src/kv/memory_manager.cc - new module implementing bins and compaction
src/kv/eviction_policy.cc - integrate hybrid scoring and call memory_manager
src/kv/spillstore_writer.cc - batch writes and compaction step
tests/kv/memory_manager_test.cc - unit tests for scoring and compaction
review_comments: Lars: Can you justify the chosen bin sizes? In our replay we saw a few bins almost always empty; consider dynamic resizing.
Asha: Good point. I exposed bin_size hints in config and added a heuristic to merge underutilized bins after N compaction cycles. Default still conservative to avoid oscillation.
Samir: The background scheduler looks solid but I'm worried about interference with RTX workloads on smaller machines. Can we gate based on GPU util and queue length?
Asha: Yes - scheduler respects two thresholds gpu_util_pct and pending_request_count. I added tests to assert scheduler pauses above thresholds.
Priya: We need more visibility into spill_batch_size distribution over time for ops; add histogram metric.
Asha: Added spill_batch_size_histogram and dashboards notes in docs. Also added alert suggestions for abnormal compaction rates.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management and eviction: adaptive compaction, hybrid eviction policy, batched spillover writes, and a background defragmentation scheduler. Results: reduced page-faults and lower tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature gated behind KV_MEMORY_MANAGER_V2. Rollout to Dedicated clusters recommended with canary.
